notes:
Undated typescript contents page headed ‘TABLE DES MATIERES’, without a grave on E, and numbered ‘- 538 -’; archive 84 is recorded in a comment. No signature, named author or total page count appears. It lists AVANT-PROPOS, INTRODUCTION, CHAPITRE O/0 .- Préliminaires and three sections with 7, 10 and 7 live numbered entries. The leader fields contain no page-number digits. The old ‘2.4. Fonctions constructibles’ and number-only ‘2.5.’ remain cancelled above their live replacements. The replacement 2.4 has no dotted leader.

The live ‘2.5?’ carries a literal typed question mark. Its role as deliberate doubt or a typing anomaly is not established. The separate marginal hook and displaced low dash may have a questioning or grouping function, which remains uncertain. The connected cancellation stroke is reproduced, and its unnamed writer is not identified from H’s descriptive note. In ‘réciproques’, the probable r under the first corrected p remains uncertain, the p under the following r is readable, and an offset terminal s impression has unresolved duplicate/correction/live-letter status. Both explicit C doubts are retained. H has description only and contributes no collation rows. No mathematical proof or computation was performed.
math_reading_decisions: The C-context title target was checked: TABLE DES MATIERES has no visible grave accent on the capital E; the unaccented spelling is retained.

The two C-context obsolete row targets were checked: 2.4. Fonctions constructibles and the following 2.5. are cancelled; the replacement 2.4 and 2.5? are live. The replacement 2.4 has no dotted leader.
The live 2.5? punctuation is a hooked typewritten question mark with a low point, not a full stop; the matter is also recorded in decision A085-05.

All section numbers, decimal reference fields, terminal points, the semicolon after Noyaux, word hyphens, apostrophes, accents, and dotted leaders were read individually. 2.10.Applications has no intervening word space after the numbering point.
The body contains no displayed or inline formulas requiring a mathematical proof check. Retaining O/0 is a glyph decision, not a claim about intended chapter numbering.

Main compared all three material readings of the terminal s from one retained word crop. The spacing, not expected French spelling, makes the single-s duplicate-impression reading preferred; the other physical alternatives remain marked.
